title: Reduce major cardiovascular events through approved obesity pharmacotherapy

concept.text: Demonstrate that an obesity medicine reduces cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction or stroke, beyond showing weight reduction. SELECT established this benefit for semaglutide in people with established cardiovascular disease and overweight or obesity, without diabetes. Proposed completion test: FDA cardiovascular-risk-reduction indication based on an event-driven randomized outcomes trial with the upper 95% confidence bound for the three-point MACE hazard ratio below 1. Test set by: FDA; SELECT prespecified the MACE composite. Its 17,604 participants supplied the decisive clinical-outcomes evidence. Reported achieved: FDA approved Wegovy's cardiovascular-risk-reduction indication on 8 March 2024; SELECT reported MACE in 6.5% versus 8.0%, hazard ratio 0.80. Overlaps: END-05, CAR-02. Sources given: [FDA cardiovascular indication announcement](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-approves-first-treatment-reduce-risk-serious-heart-problems-specifically-adults-obesity-or) ; [FDA Wegovy label with SELECT results](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2024/215256s015lbl.pdf).

page.title: First obesity medicine approved to reduce major cardiovascular events
page.definition: A regulator approves a weight-management medicine to reduce major cardiovascular events in adults with established cardiovascular disease and either overweight or obesity. The pivotal trial measured time to the first of three events: cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction (heart attack) or nonfatal stroke. This use is secondary prevention. The US indication applies regardless of diabetes status and specifies use with a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity.

goal.need: In 2022, an estimated 7.9 million US adults aged 45 or older had cardiovascular disease, a body mass index of at least 27 kg/m² and no diabetes. In a trial of such patients receiving usual care, including blood pressure and cholesterol management, 8.0% on placebo experienced cardiovascular death, nonfatal heart attack or nonfatal stroke over a mean 39.8 months, compared with 6.5% on semaglutide. The trial did not establish a reduction in cardiovascular death alone. Weight loss can accompany harm: sibutramine reduced weight but increased nonfatal heart attacks and strokes in high-risk adults.

figures.caption: Cardiovascular outcomes in SCOUT, published on 2 September 2010.
figures.note: Mean treatment duration was 3.4 years. The composite included cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke and resuscitation after cardiac arrest.

statements.quote: Novo Nordisk also plans to initiate a cardiovascular outcomes study SELECT in approximately 17,500 people who are overweight or have obesity.
statements.context: The company's semaglutide obesity development programme.

statements.quote: Providing a treatment option that is proven to lower this cardiovascular risk is a major advance for public health.
statements.context: John Sharretts, director of FDA's Division of Diabetes, Lipid Disorders, and Obesity, discussing cardiovascular risk in adults with cardiovascular disease and overweight or obesity.

statements.quote: lowers the incidence of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) versus semaglutide placebo
statements.context: SELECT’s primary objective was to demonstrate this benefit for once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide 2.4 mg, with both groups receiving standard care.

statements.body: European Medicines Agency, Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use
statements.quote: Therefore, no separate indication for the prevention of cardiovascular disease in people with obesity and overweight is needed.
statements.context: The committee accepted the reduction in major cardiovascular events and considered patients with established cardiovascular disease and a body mass index of at least 27 kg/m² already covered by the weight-management indication.

completion.title: A regulator approves the first weight-management medicine indicated to reduce major cardiovascular events.
completion.criterion: A medicines regulator grants a product approved for chronic weight management an explicit indication to reduce the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events in adults with established cardiovascular disease and overweight or obesity. The outcome comprises cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction or nonfatal stroke. The approval must name cardiovascular risk reduction as an authorised use.
completion.set_by: Medicines regulators granting the indication, including the US Food and Drug Administration under NDA 215256/S-011 and the UK Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency.
completion.threshold_quote: Wegovy is indicated in combination with a reduced calorie diet and increased physical activity to reduce the risk of major adverse cardiovascular events (cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, or non-fatal stroke) in adults with established cardiovascular disease and either obesity or overweight.
completion.basis: On 8 March 2024 the FDA identified Wegovy injection as the first weight-loss medication with this US approval. SELECT supplied the evidence. Its age cutoff of 45 years, body mass index cutoff of 27 kg/m² and exclusion of diabetes were trial eligibility rules. The UK granted a prevention indication on 23 July 2024. The European Medicines Agency accepted the results for inclusion in the product information and declined a separate indication.

milestones.criterion: The investigational new drug application contains adequate information from pharmacological and toxicological studies in laboratory animals or in vitro to support the sponsor’s conclusion that the proposed clinical investigations are reasonably safe.

milestones.title: A participant receives the first human dose of the candidate medicine in a phase 1 study.
milestones.criterion: At least one participant receives the investigational medicine in a first-in-human phase 1 study. The study may enrol healthy volunteers or patients.
milestones.set_by: U.S. Food and Drug Administration, 21 CFR 312.21(a)(1).
milestones.threshold_quote: Phase 1 includes the initial introduction of an investigational new drug into humans.

milestones.title: Semaglutide is superior to placebo on both STEP 1 weight endpoints at 68 weeks, with two-sided P<0.05.
milestones.criterion: In STEP 1, compare once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide 2.4 mg with placebo, each with lifestyle intervention, in adults without diabetes who have a body mass index of at least 30 kg/m², or at least 27 kg/m² with a weight-related condition. At week 68, both the mean percentage change in weight and the proportion losing at least 5% of baseline weight must favour semaglutide at two-sided P<0.05 in the prespecified testing sequence. The primary analysis includes participants regardless of treatment discontinuation or rescue intervention.
milestones.set_by: Novo Nordisk A/S, STEP 1 statistical analysis plan, NCT03548935.
milestones.threshold_quote: Superiority will be claimed if p-values are less than 5% and the estimated treatment contrasts favours semaglutide 2.4 mg.

milestones.title: An obesity medicine receives FDA approval for chronic weight management.
milestones.criterion: FDA approves the medicine for chronic weight management as an adjunct to a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity in adults with an initial body mass index of at least 30 kg/m², or at least 27 kg/m² with at least one weight-related condition. Body mass index is weight in kilograms divided by height in metres squared.
milestones.set_by: U.S. Food and Drug Administration, original Wegovy approval NDA 215256 and prescribing information, section 1; these eligibility thresholds are from the adult semaglutide indication.
milestones.threshold_quote:
30 kg/m2 or greater (obesity) or
• 27 kg/m2 or greater (overweight) in the presence of at least one weight-related comorbid condition

milestones.title: Semaglutide lowers the risk of a first major cardiovascular event in SELECT at two-sided P<0.046.
milestones.criterion: SELECT compares weekly subcutaneous semaglutide 2.4 mg with placebo, each added to standard care, in adults aged at least 45 with body mass index at least 27 kg/m², established cardiovascular disease and no diabetes. The primary endpoint is time to first cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction or nonfatal stroke. At the final analysis the comparison must favour semaglutide and cross the nominal two-sided P<0.046 boundary. The group-sequential design controls overall one-sided type I error at 0.025.
milestones.set_by: Novo Nordisk and the SELECT steering committee, NCT03574597 statistical analysis plan and the final nominal boundary reported in Table 2 of the trial publication.
milestones.threshold_quote: the nominal two-sided significance level was 0.046.

milestones.title: A phase 2 trial measures 52-week weight change at five daily semaglutide doses against placebo.
milestones.criterion: In adults with obesity, a body mass index of at least 30 kg/m² and no diabetes, compare percentage change in body weight from baseline to week 52 for five once-daily subcutaneous semaglutide doses (0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3 and 0.4 mg) against pooled placebo. The primary analysis compares each dose on the four-week escalation schedule with placebo and adjusts for the five comparisons.
milestones.set_by: Novo Nordisk A/S, phase 2 dose-ranging protocol NCT02453711.
milestones.threshold_quote: To assess and compare the dose-response of five doses of once-daily semaglutide versus placebo in inducing and maintaining weight loss after 52 weeks

results.finding: Semaglutide repeat-dose toxicity in rats (sample size unreported) had a no-observed-adverse-effect level of 0.6 mg/kg/day.
results.detail: The rat study lasted at least 26 weeks. The later NDA review summarizes the nonclinical program and leaves the timing and adequacy of the initial IND package unresolved.
results.quote:
The 
NOAEL for this study was the highest dose examined (0.6 mg/kg/day, 10-fold the 
MRHD).

results.finding: FDA's nonclinical review supported semaglutide for chronic weight management at a proposed 2.4 mg/week (no single study sample size).
results.detail: The signed review records the nonclinical approvability recommendation for NDA 215256.
results.quote:
The nonclinical data support market approval of subcutaneously administered 
semaglutide as an adjunct to a reduced calorie meal plan and increased physical 
activity for chronic weight management in adult patients with obesity or excess weight.

results.finding: Subcutaneous semaglutide had a CNS no-observed-adverse-effect level of 22 µg/kg in rats (sample size unreported).
results.detail: The CHMP's sufficiency conclusion applies to the marketing dossier. The rat CNS study provides one result from the broader nonclinical program.
results.quote: The No Observed Adverse Effect Level (NOAEL) was determined to be 22 µg/kg.

results.finding: First-in-human phase 1 study 1820 of semaglutide included 56 healthy men in the full analysis set and recorded exposure after dosing.
results.detail: The full analysis set count is for the study as a whole. The report does not give a semaglutide-only count in the supplied text.

results.finding: In STEP 1 (n=1,961), semaglutide was superior to placebo on both week-68 weight endpoints (two-sided P<0.001 for each).
results.detail: The observed responder percentages used week-68 data from 1,212 semaglutide and 577 placebo participants. The primary hypothesis test used the full randomized population with multiple imputation for missing data.
results.quote:
The mean change in body weight from baseline to week 68 was −14.9% in the 
semaglutide group as compared with −2.4% with placebo, for an estimated treatment 
difference of −12.4 percentage points (95% confidence interval [CI], −13.4 to −11.5; 
P<0.001).

results.finding: FDA approved Wegovy for chronic weight management on June 4, 2021. Sample size is inapplicable to the approval decision.
results.detail: The approval package identifies the decision as NDA 215256.
results.quote:
We have completed our review of this application, as amended. It is approved, effective 
on the date of this letter, for use as recommended in the enclosed agreed-upon 
labeling.

results.finding: In SELECT (n=17,604), semaglutide lowered the risk of a first major cardiovascular event versus placebo (two-sided P<0.001).
results.quote:
A primary cardiovascular end-point event occurred in 569 of the 
8803 patients (6.5%) in the semaglutide group and in 701 of the 8801 patients 
(8.0%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.80; 95% confidence interval, 0.72 to 
0.90; P<0.001).

results.finding: FDA approved Wegovy for cardiovascular risk reduction on March 8, 2024, based on SELECT (~17,500 patients in the trial description).
results.detail: The sample size is the approximate enrollment specified in the postmarketing requirement. FDA's approval was effective on the date of the letter.
results.quote:
We have completed our review of this application, as amended. It is approved, effective 
on the date of this letter, for use as recommended in the enclosed agreed-upon labeling 
with minor editorial revisions listed below and reflected in the enclosed labeling.
